question:
A 63-year-old male presents with severe anal pain that started 2 hours ago. He has a history of chronic
constipation but no other significant medical conditions and takes no medications. His vital signs are
normal. Rectal examination under local anesthesia reveals a palpable perianal mass without evidence
of a skin tag or mucosal prolapse through the anal canal. What is the most appropriate immediate
management for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Lateral internal sphincterotomy (B) Application of
topical hydrocortisone (C) Sclerotherapy injection (D) Hemorrhoidectomy (E) Elliptical excision (F)
Fistulotomy (G) Conservative management with sitz baths (H) Topical nitroglycerin application (I)
Rubber band ligation (J) Incision and drainage
 A. Application of topical hydrocortisone
B. Elliptical excision
C. Conservative management with sitz baths
D. Sclerotherapy injection
E. Incision and drainage
F. Rubber band ligation
G. Hemorrhoidectomy
H. Fistulotomy
I. Topical nitroglycerin application
J. Lateral internal sphincterotomy
